summary.oneLiner: Diversified heavy-engineering player split into a steady, high-margin **Manufacturing** business (12–13% EBIT, 3 yrs running) and a lower-margin, lumpier **Projects/EPC** business (4.58% EBIT FY26, guided to ~5.5% FY27). FY26 standalone was soft (rev +4.2%, below own 7–8% guide) but Q4 recovered hard (rev +16%, PBT +48% YoY). The big structural positives: **exports doubled to INR1,169 cr (22% of rev)** with rising market share, net debt halved, and order book healthy at ~INR7,000 cr opening FY27. The big overhang: the **Philippines ethanol asset (CBPI)** — reclassified from "held for sale" to continuing operations, dragging consolidated PAT down 25% via a INR104 cr depreciation catch-up and forex noise, though now operationally cash-positive. FY27 standalone growth guided 10–12%, led by manufacturing.

scorecard:
| Metric | FY26 | YoY / Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Standalone Revenue** | INR5,229 cr | +4.2% YoY (below own 7–8% guide); Q4 rev +16% YoY |
| **Standalone PBT (reported)** | INR455 cr | +17% YoY; Q4 PBT +48% YoY |
| **Standalone PBT (normalized)** | ~INR375 cr | Excl. ~INR80 cr Philippines-related items → broadly flat YoY operationally |
| **Mfg EBIT margin** | 12.46% | Within 12–13% guided band (3 yrs running) |
| **Projects/EPC EBIT margin** | 4.58% | Guided to ~5.5% in FY27 |
| **Export revenue** | INR1,169 cr (~22% of rev) | Up from INR532 cr (~14%) — more than doubled YoY |
| **Consol EBITDA** | INR671 cr | +19% YoY (vs INR566 cr) |
| **Consol PAT** | INR154 cr | −25% YoY (vs INR204 cr) — hit by Philippines depreciation catch-up |
| **Consol depreciation** | INR278 cr | +INR104 cr YoY (Philippines catch-up on reclassification) |
| **Consol Net borrowings** | INR476 cr | Down from INR836 cr — improved substantially |
| **Standalone cash & equiv** | INR241 cr (31-Mar-26) | After funding ~INR150 cr capex from internal accruals |
| **Capex (FY26)** | INR153 cr | Capacity additions across most mfg lines |
| **Dividend** | INR6/share | +20% YoY |

**One-offs / non-operational (FLAGGED):**
- ~INR80 cr of standalone PBT from Philippines-related items — real P&L but **not core operational earnings**; underlying operational PBT ~INR375 cr.
- Consol depreciation includes **INR104 cr YoY increase** = catch-up charge on Philippines (CBPI) assets reclassified from held-for-sale to continuing operations.
- CBPI full-year reported loss INR295 cr = INR170 cr depreciation + INR95 cr forex variation (nets off vs ISGEC) + ~INR70 cr interest accrual + ~INR26 cr genuine operational loss (plant ran only 3.5 months).
- Consol other income includes INR103 cr forex fluctuation gain; ~INR50 cr+ corresponding offset sits in other expenses (Isgec Investments Pte Ltd, Singapore) — gross-up per accounting standards.
- Other income parts: interest/net gain on current investments; government grants (Saraswati Sugar Mills); forex (Eagle Press + Singapore subsidiary).
guidance (critical):
- **FY27 standalone revenue: +10% to +12%.** Bulk from Manufacturing — ~INR500 cr / ~10% from mfg; Projects only ~3–4% growth.
- **Mfg EBIT margin: 12–13%** maintained (confident; back-to-back supplier orders + contingency margins hedge input-cost inflation).
- **Projects/EPC EBIT margin: ~5.5% in FY27** (up from 4.58%) — older orders completing, newer orders booked at better margins, shorter-gestation projects.
- **Order book:** opening FY27 ~INR7,000 cr (after excluding 2 cancelled orders worth ~INR550 cr). First 2 months of current quarter: new orders ~INR1,400 cr booked.
- **Mfg vs EPC mix:** growth tilted strongly to manufacturing.
- **Exports:** expect FY27 export revenue "a little more than" INR1,100–1,200 cr; export order book % to rise; weaker INR supports realizations.
- **Isgec Hitachi Zosen JV (FY27):** revenue ~INR700 cr, PBT INR100 cr+ (vs FY26 Total Income INR672 cr, PBT INR103 cr).
- **CBPI/Philippines (FY27):** plant running 70–75% now, targeting 85–90% utilization (ex ~1–1.5 months of heavy rain); cash-positive, self-sustaining, no further funding needed; depreciation ~INR150 cr (down from INR170 cr); no EBITDA number given.
order book & pipeline (segment split):
- **Opening FY27 order book: ~INR7,000 cr** (standalone, post excluding INR550 cr cancellations).
- **Export order book: ~INR1,450 cr** as on 31-Mar-2026 (expected to rise as % over FY27).
- **New orders booked Apr–May FY27: ~INR1,400 cr** (includes some export orders).
- **Isgec Hitachi Zosen orders in hand: INR763 cr** (31-Mar-2026); strong execution.
- **Cancellations:** 2 orders worth ~INR550 cr cancelled during FY26 (excluded from opening book).
- Inquiry pipeline "strong" in both domestic and export markets.
segment (manufacturing vs epc):
- **Manufacturing:** revenue booked on dispatch (sale-of-goods method) → quarter-to-quarter lumpy (Q3 strong, Q4 moderated purely on order/dispatch mix, not cost pressure). EBIT 12.46% FY26. New export markets for **presses in SE Asia** (Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia). Steel castings expansion approved (Muzaffarnagar, +INR25 cr).
- **Projects/EPC:** EBIT 4.58% FY26; pivot (started ~1.5–2 yrs ago) from long-gestation to **shorter-gestation projects** is reducing working capital and execution risk → supports the ~5.5% FY27 margin. Geographies: developing countries — recent wins in **Africa and Latin America**.
growth / optionality:
- **Exports** as the structural growth engine — market-share gains in presses (SE Asia) and projects (Africa, LatAm); weaker INR a tailwind.
- **New-technology equipment plays:** ISGEC supplies equipment used in **coal gasification** and **polysilicon-to-wafer (solar)** value chains — already won equipment orders; "play in some part of the value chain."
- **Capacity additions coming online in FY27** to contribute to revenue.
- **CBPI ethanol** turning self-sustaining/cash-positive — optional value on eventual sale (running plant easier to sell).
- Diverse end-markets doing well: Sugar, Power, Oil & Gas, Automobiles, Fertilizers. Weak: paper; few new India ethanol plants.
margins & cost:
- Mfg 12–13% defended via back-to-back supplier orders placed soon after customer orders + contingency margins.
- **Input-cost inflation flagged:** steel forgings, castings, chemicals, certain imported materials; gas shortages raising fuel costs; longer/costlier export-import logistics. Most expected to be absorbed via normal contingency provisions.
- EPC margin lift driven by old-project completion + better-priced shorter new orders.
capex:
- FY26 capex INR153 cr (some references to ~INR150 cr), funded from internal accruals.
- Capacity additions across most manufacturing product lines — "on schedule with minor adjustments."
- **Board approved +INR25 cr** to expand Muzaffarnagar steel castings plant.
capital allocation:
- Net borrowings (consol) cut from INR836 cr → INR476 cr.
- Standalone: no working-capital borrowings; borrowings are on-lent to CBPI (shareholder-loan style funding of Philippines unit).
- Dividend INR6/share (+20% YoY).
- FGD retention money: >INR200 cr of the ~INR300 cr expected was realized; INR165 cr still outstanding (one-third expected in June, rest by August).
- Capex funded internally; cash & equiv INR241 cr at year-end.
risks (epc execution / margins):
- **Projects/EPC margin uncertainty** tied to geopolitical/war situation; mgmt "doesn't know when war will end."
- **Input-cost inflation** (steel, castings, forgings, imports, gas/fuel, logistics) — partially hedged, not fully eliminated.
- **Philippines/CBPI overhang:** no longer held-for-sale; sale timing uncertain (1–2 yrs hoped); prior deal collapsed (buyer couldn't fund). Depreciation/forex drag on consolidated PAT.
- **Subsidiary "capital deficiency"** (negative net worth) in Isgec Investments Pte Ltd & Bioeq Energy Holding — mgmt says immaterial as all borrowings are intra-group (shareholder loans).
- **Export receivables / FX risk** in Africa/LatAm — mitigated via confirmed LCs (USD/EUR), forward covers, and running cash-surplus payment schedules.
- Order cancellations (INR550 cr in FY26) show book is not immune.
mgmt tone: Transparent and measured. Proactively disclosed the INR80 cr non-operational PBT component and the underlying ~INR375 cr "true" PBT; candidly admitted FY26 missed its own 7–8% revenue guide; detailed the CBPI loss bridge line-by-line. Confident on manufacturing margins and exports; cautious/conditional on EPC margins and Philippines sale. Analysts praised the regular, detailed disclosure.
non-obvious:
- Manufacturing revenue is dispatch-based, so quarterly mfg margins/revenue are noise — **annual view required** (mgmt explicit).
- Reclassifying CBPI from "held for sale" to "continuing operations" is what mechanically crushed consol PAT (INR104 cr depreciation catch-up), not an operational deterioration.
- CBPI ethanol sales gated by **Philippine govt (Dept of Energy) allocations** per factory; allocations for Apr–Jun and Jul–Sep quarters → Q4 had almost no ethanol sales despite production (ethanol stocked). Already sold 4.35 million litres Apr–May FY27; contracts with ~6 Philippine oil companies (all blend/import, no refining).
- ~INR80 cr of standalone PBT is Philippines-related — flatters standalone optics.
- Forex gross-up (INR103 cr other income vs ~INR50 cr+ in other expenses) is presentation, not economic.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ⭐ **ISGEC itself** a beneficiary of: weaker INR (export realizations), post-COVID export push paying off (SE Asia presses, Africa/LatAm projects), and new-tech equipment demand (coal gasification, polysilicon-to-wafer/solar).
- ✅ Shorter-gestation EPC model → better working capital + margins.
- (Specific external beneficiary tickers — none identified in transcript.)

themes.title: Capital-goods & machine-tool import-substitution
themes.need: Atmanirbhar machine-tool and heavy-engineering localization is supply-constrained against import-substituting demand. JYOTICNC runs >100% utilization with a INR4,732cr order book and near-triples capacity; ELGIEQUIP/CUMMINSIND/ELECON/LMW ride the same capex + export + China+1 pull; ISGEC/BHEL/GMMPFAUDLR/KIRLPNU on process + energy capex.
themes.driver: Capacity expansion going live (JYOTICNC); defence/EMS order conversion; US-reshoring export demand (ELGIEQUIP).

themes.title: Bioenergy / Ethanol / SAF transition
themes.need: Higher ethanol-blending mandates (E20->E25/E27/E30), CBG, SAF and bio-IBA underpin a multi-year bioenergy capex cycle. PRAJIND's near-term earnings are depressed by a 1G slowdown + GenX gestation but the optionality (SAF, CBG, DC-cooling) is large; TRUALT/BALRAMCHIN/EIDPARRY/TRIVENI/GODAVARIB add ethanol/sugar; BCLIND/GULPOLY/GLOBUSSPR on grain-based distillation.
themes.driver: Higher blending-mandate notifications; SAF/CBG order conversion; sugar-cycle realisations.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "93+ Years & Going Strong": incorporated in 1933 as a sugar manufacturing company (then Saraswati Sugar Syndicate Ltd.) and "Transformed into a Diversified Heavy Engineering Company with 87% Consolidated Revenue* from Engineering Products and Projects" (*FY25 Consolidated Revenue).
- Deck claims "Global Reach with Clients across 99 Countries, 6 continents" and equipment supplied in 99 countries; marquee clientele slide names bp, ExxonMobil, Reliance, IndianOil, Bharat Petroleum, SAIL, Siemens, Alstom, Toyota, Maruti Suzuki, Vedanta, Adani Wilmar, Dalmia Bharat, Thyssenkrupp, Aditya Birla Group, Technip, Mitsubishi, Toyo Engineering, RITES, Air Products and Mahindra.
- "Robust Order Book & Strong Credit Profile (AA Stable and A1+ by ICRA)".
- Order book of Rs. 89,580 Mn as on 30th June 2026 is described as "Comfortably placed to counter the Cyclicality of any specific industry", spread across Power, Sugar, Automobile, Refineries, Chemicals & Fertilizers, Steel/Cement/Aluminium and Others.
- Cover slide cites "One of the world's largest cement waste heat recovery boilers, generating 34.5 MW of power from a single line".

guidance.body:
- **FY27 standalone revenue: +10% to +12%.** Bulk from Manufacturing — ~INR500 cr / ~10% from mfg; Projects only ~3–4% growth.
- **Mfg EBIT margin: 12–13%** maintained (confident; back-to-back supplier orders + contingency margins hedge input-cost inflation).
- **Projects/EPC EBIT margin: ~5.5% in FY27** (up from 4.58%) — older orders completing, newer orders booked at better margins, shorter-gestation projects.
- **Order book:** opening FY27 ~INR7,000 cr (after excluding 2 cancelled orders worth ~INR550 cr). First 2 months of current quarter: new orders ~INR1,400 cr booked.
- **Mfg vs EPC mix:** growth tilted strongly to manufacturing.
- **Exports:** expect FY27 export revenue "a little more than" INR1,100–1,200 cr; export order book % to rise; weaker INR supports realizations.
- **Isgec Hitachi Zosen JV (FY27):** revenue ~INR700 cr, PBT INR100 cr+ (vs FY26 Total Income INR672 cr, PBT INR103 cr).
- **CBPI/Philippines (FY27):** plant running 70–75% now, targeting 85–90% utilization (ex ~1–1.5 months of heavy rain); cash-positive, self-sustaining, no further funding needed; depreciation ~INR150 cr (down from INR170 cr); no EBITDA number given.

growth_optionality.title: Growth / Optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Exports** as the structural growth engine — market-share gains in presses (SE Asia) and projects (Africa, LatAm); weaker INR a tailwind.
- **New-technology equipment plays:** ISGEC supplies equipment used in **coal gasification** and **polysilicon-to-wafer (solar)** value chains — already won equipment orders; "play in some part of the value chain."
- **Capacity additions coming online in FY27** to contribute to revenue.
- **CBPI ethanol** turning self-sustaining/cash-positive — optional value on eventual sale (running plant easier to sell).
- Diverse end-markets doing well: Sugar, Power, Oil & Gas, Automobiles, Fertilizers. Weak: paper; few new India ethanol plants.

margins.title: Margins & Cost
margins.body:
- Mfg 12–13% defended via back-to-back supplier orders placed soon after customer orders + contingency margins.
- **Input-cost inflation flagged:** steel forgings, castings, chemicals, certain imported materials; gas shortages raising fuel costs; longer/costlier export-import logistics. Most expected to be absorbed via normal contingency provisions.
- EPC margin lift driven by old-project completion + better-priced shorter new orders.

capital_allocation.title: Capital Allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Net borrowings (consol) cut from INR836 cr → INR476 cr.
- Standalone: no working-capital borrowings; borrowings are on-lent to CBPI (shareholder-loan style funding of Philippines unit).
- Dividend INR6/share (+20% YoY).
- FGD retention money: >INR200 cr of the ~INR300 cr expected was realized; INR165 cr still outstanding (one-third expected in June, rest by August).
- Capex funded internally; cash & equiv INR241 cr at year-end.

management_tone.title: Mgmt Tone
management_tone.body: Transparent and measured. Proactively disclosed the INR80 cr non-operational PBT component and the underlying ~INR375 cr "true" PBT; candidly admitted FY26 missed its own 7–8% revenue guide; detailed the CBPI loss bridge line-by-line. Confident on manufacturing margins and exports; cautious/conditional on EPC margins and Philippines sale. Analysts praised the regular, detailed disclosure.

risks.title: Risks (EPC execution / margins)
risks.body:
- **Projects/EPC margin uncertainty** tied to geopolitical/war situation; mgmt "doesn't know when war will end."
- **Input-cost inflation** (steel, castings, forgings, imports, gas/fuel, logistics) — partially hedged, not fully eliminated.
- **Philippines/CBPI overhang:** no longer held-for-sale; sale timing uncertain (1–2 yrs hoped); prior deal collapsed (buyer couldn't fund). Depreciation/forex drag on consolidated PAT.
- **Subsidiary "capital deficiency"** (negative net worth) in Isgec Investments Pte Ltd & Bioeq Energy Holding — mgmt says immaterial as all borrowings are intra-group (shareholder loans).
- **Export receivables / FX risk** in Africa/LatAm — mitigated via confirmed LCs (USD/EUR), forward covers, and running cash-surplus payment schedules.
- Order cancellations (INR550 cr in FY26) show book is not immune.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious
non_obvious.body:
- Manufacturing revenue is dispatch-based, so quarterly mfg margins/revenue are noise — **annual view required** (mgmt explicit).
- Reclassifying CBPI from "held for sale" to "continuing operations" is what mechanically crushed consol PAT (INR104 cr depreciation catch-up), not an operational deterioration.
- CBPI ethanol sales gated by **Philippine govt (Dept of Energy) allocations** per factory; allocations for Apr–Jun and Jul–Sep quarters → Q4 had almost no ethanol sales despite production (ethanol stocked). Already sold 4.35 million litres Apr–May FY27; contracts with ~6 Philippine oil companies (all blend/import, no refining).
- ~INR80 cr of standalone PBT is Philippines-related — flatters standalone optics.
- Forex gross-up (INR103 cr other income vs ~INR50 cr+ in other expenses) is presentation, not economic.

challenges.title: Challenges → Beneficiaries
challenges.body:
- ⭐ **ISGEC itself** a beneficiary of: weaker INR (export realizations), post-COVID export push paying off (SE Asia presses, Africa/LatAm projects), and new-tech equipment demand (coal gasification, polysilicon-to-wafer/solar).
- ✅ Shorter-gestation EPC model → better working capital + margins.
- (Specific external beneficiary tickers — none identified in transcript.)

qoq_log.title: QoQ Log
qoq_log.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Standalone rev +4.2% FY26 to INR5,229 cr (Q4 +16% YoY); reported PBT INR455 cr (+17%), normalized ~INR375 cr (~INR80 cr Philippines items excluded). Mfg EBIT 12.46%, EPC EBIT 4.58%. Exports doubled to INR1,169 cr (22%). Consol EBITDA INR671 cr (+19%); Consol PAT INR154 cr (−25%, Philippines depreciation catch-up +INR104 cr). Net debt INR476 cr (from INR836 cr). Order book ~INR7,000 cr opening FY27; +INR1,400 cr booked Apr–May; export book INR1,450 cr. Isgec Hitachi Zosen FY26 income INR672 cr / PBT INR103 cr; order book INR763 cr. CBPI reclassified to continuing ops, now cash-positive. FY27 guide: rev +10–12%, mfg margin 12–13%, EPC ~5.5%. Capex INR153 cr; dividend INR6/sh (+20%).
- _Prior quarters: not covered in this transcript (single-call source). Q3 FY26 mfg margins noted as "exceptionally strong" vs Q4 moderation (dispatch-mix driven). Earlier call had guided 7–8% FY26 revenue (missed). Prior quarter flagged ~INR300 cr FGD retention release expected in Q4 (>INR200 cr realized; INR165 cr outstanding)._
